title: Maximum XOR With an Element From Array
summary: Given an array of non-negative integers and a queries array, for each query, find the maximum bitwise XOR of the query's first element with any array element that does not exceed the query's second element.
statement: Given an array of non-negative integers and a queries array, for each query, find the maximum bitwise XOR of the query's first element with any array element that does not exceed the query's second element. If no array element meets the condition, return -1. Return an array of answers corresponding to each query.
constraints: nums and queries each contain up to 100000 entries; all values and limits are between zero and 10^9.
For query [x,m], choose a nums value no greater than m that maximizes x XOR value.
Return -1 for a query with no eligible value, preserving query order.
hints: Sort queries by limit so eligible numbers can be inserted once in increasing order.
Store inserted numbers in a binary trie from the highest relevant bit downward.
For each x bit, prefer the opposite trie branch to set that result bit; fall back to the matching branch.
At a query’s turn the trie contains exactly nums values no greater than its limit, and greedy highest-bit choices lexicographically maximize the XOR value.
editorial: Sort nums and process queries offline by m. Incrementally insert newly eligible values into a binary trie. A query greedily takes the opposite bit whenever possible from bit 30 down, which maximizes the most significant differing bit before lower bits matter. Restore answers to original query order. The oracle independently enumerates every eligible number.

tests.explanation: Eligible maxima are three, three, and seven for the three queries respectively.
The first query can use up to four and reaches fifteen; the second has no eligible value; the third reaches five.
